title: The @ prefix is not part of the saved name and never appears twice
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Notifications page opens from the bell icon at the top right, next to your location name.
  2. Open the Notifications page from the bell and select the Tag groups tab. An active location is selected (the location name shown next to the bell; change it with your initials at the top right -> Change Location).
custom_steps:
1. Click the bell icon at the top right and open the Tag groups tab. Create a group (e.g. name "Service Team") and check what is saved/listed/duplicate-checked (typed text only, no @).
  2. Type 40 characters after the @ and confirm all are accepted.
  3. Type @ as the first character; then type @ later in the name.
  4. Open the Edit dialog on a group whose stored name begins with @.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The @ is not part of the group's name - what saves, lists, is duplicate-checked and shows elsewhere is the typed text alone, with no @; and the @ does not count toward the 40-character limit (you can type 40 after it).
  • Typing @ as the first character does not insert it (the field never shows two), while a @ typed anywhere else is accepted as an ordinary character.
  • When Edit opens on a group whose stored name begins with @, that leading @ is not shown in the typing area (the fixed prefix supplies it) and saving stores the name without it.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667; story SV-10249 (S6, Manage tag groups); Notifications Update v1 PRD (Confluence 817463297), S6; design boards TagGroups/Modal; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-R8d: “The @ is not part of the group's name. The name saved, listed on the Tag groups tab, checked for duplicates and shown anywhere else in the product is the typed text alone, with no @.”
  • S6-R8e: “The @ does not count toward the 40-character limit in S6-R8. A user can type 40 characters after it.”
  • S6-R8f: “If the user types @ as the first character of the name, it is not inserted. The field never shows two of them.”
  • S6-R8g: “A @ typed anywhere other than the first position is accepted as an ordinary character, because it is part of the name the user chose.”
  • S6-R8h: “When the Edit dialog opens on a group whose stored name begins with @, that leading @ is not shown in the typing area, because the fixed prefix already supplies it. Saving stores the name without it.”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.
